intro.author: The apostle Peter (1:1), writing 'by Silvanus' (5:12), who may have helped write the letter or carried it. Some scholars question whether Peter wrote it, partly because of its polished Greek; others see Silvanus's help as the explanation.
intro.written: If by Peter, about AD 62–64, from 'Babylon' (5:13), widely understood as a code name for Rome, shortly before Peter's death under Nero
intro.audience: 'Strangers scattered' through five Roman provinces in Asia Minor: Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia (1:1), many of them former pagans (4:3)
intro.setting: These believers were being slandered and mistreated by neighbors who resented their refusal to join old pagan habits and festivities (4:3-4). The suffering seems to have been mostly local and social rather than an official, empire-wide persecution. Peter calls them God's chosen exiles, applying to them language once used of scattered Israel.
intro.purpose: Peter encourages suffering believers to stand firm in God's grace, to live honorably among outsiders, and to follow Christ's example of suffering with hope.
intro.bigIdea: God's chosen exiles can endure suffering with hope, following Christ, because glory is coming.

outline.title: A living hope and a holy people

commentary.t: THE FIRST EPISTLE GENERAL OF PETER
